findings.title: No Redis-first run-sale eligibility gate on the buy hot path
findings.summary: The atomic Lua gate decides eligibility solely from inventory-key existence and never validates the request runId against the offer's owning run or lifecycle. A wrong-runId buy decrements Redis stock, is rejected by the ownership trigger, and lands as a pending hold that can never reconcile — permanently leaked stock. Finalized runs' offers also remain buyable, going stale against their written summaries.

findings.title: Realtime publications are awaited synchronously on the buy hot path in production
findings.summary: Every accepted reservation serializes several awaited publishes plus redundant Redis reads (an extra inventory-state read and queue.getJobCounts) before responding — despite the modules' own notes saying publication would switch to fire-and-forget once a real channel was wired, which has now happened.

findings.title: Startup reconciliation reports a run as reconciled even when it did not fail it
findings.summary: When the guarded UPDATE matches zero rows (a concurrent transition won), the loop still pushes the run into the reconciled array, so the dashboard receives a spurious run.failed SSE event for a run that continues to drain and finalize normally.

findings.title: getRunSecuredVsConfirmed counts all reservation statuses, not just secured
findings.summary: The query has no status filter, unlike its documented semantic and the sibling order counts. Correct today because only secured rows are ever written, but acceptedReservations silently inflates the moment a release/expiry transition lands.

findings.title: Preset mutation adapters return preset_not_found for a config-validation failure
findings.summary: save/duplicate/copy-to-custom each map a defensive schema-parse failure to preset_not_found, so an invalid config would surface as a misleading 404 rather than a validation error.

findings.title: seedDemoData silently overwrites admin/API-owned editable rows on every re-run
findings.summary: onConflictDoUpdate unconditionally rewrites the active public runtime policy and every editable admin preset (including the admin-custom scratch) back to hardcoded defaults, discarding operator edits without warning on any runtime:setup re-run.

findings.title: Run-scoped ERP behavior and backpressure captured in the run snapshot are never applied
findings.summary: erpConfig and backpressureConfig are frozen into the snapshot, cap-validated, and rendered on the dashboard, but the mock ERP resolves only its retained global control and the worker reads every resilience/concurrency knob from env — the documented run-scoped behavior is dead configuration and global chaos leaks between runs structurally.

findings.title: Circuit breaker half-open allows multiple concurrent trial calls, not a single trial
findings.summary: The half_open branch returns true for every call while the inline comment claims a single trial, so up to worker-concurrency confirmations hit a still-failing ERP during each recovery probe.

findings.title: Production worker has no BullMQ retry; unexpected throws strand orders in processing
findings.summary: Neither producer nor consumer configures BullMQ attempts, while code comments and the async-pipeline tests assume retries exist; an unexpected throw fails the job after one attempt and leaves the order permanently in processing.

findings.title: Finalization writes the summary and the lifecycle transition non-atomically; the already_finalized early-return then strands the run in draining forever
findings.summary: A crash or transient DB error between the summary write and completeRun/failRun leaves a summary present with the run still draining; every later poller tick then early-returns already_finalized without retrying the transition. The stranded run survives restarts and blocks all future starts until an admin reset — and the idempotency test codifies the faulty assumption.

findings.title: trafficDeliveryStatus carries mixed execution-vs-delivery vocabulary across lifecycle events; the classified delivery status is computed on the draining path and then discarded
findings.summary: run.active/run.draining events populate the field with orchestrator execution status while terminal events use the API-classified delivery vocabulary; on the draining path the classified summary is computed and used only in a log line.

findings.title: The one-current-run start gate is a TOCTOU read-then-write; concurrent starts can create two overlapping runs
findings.summary: canStartRun is a plain SELECT and the starting row is inserted much later with no guard, so two start requests that both pass the gate produce two recoverable runs — two k6 processes, split inventory accounting, ambiguous recovery.

findings.title: The finalization poller does not serialize ticks; slow finalization lets overlapping ticks race on the same draining run
findings.summary: setInterval fires on a fixed cadence with fire-and-forget ticks; overlapping ticks are mostly benign under the idempotent guards but widen the Finding 10 window and multiply redundant reads.

findings.title: k6 metrics streaming re-reads and re-parses the whole output file every window (quadratic in run length); a partially-written line can be dropped from an intermediate window
findings.summary: Each 1s flush re-reads the entire growing NDJSON file and slices by positional count, so parsing grows quadratically with run length, and a line partial in one window and complete in the next can be skipped. The terminal summary is unaffected.

findings.title: Finalization does not wait for post-confirmation notifications, so a run can finalize while notifications are still missing and notificationsRecorded undercounts
findings.summary: The settled gate covers queued/processing orders and pending holds but not notifications, which are recorded best-effort after confirmed — so the immutable summary's notificationsRecorded is a point-in-time count, not a settled guarantee.

findings.title: Live Watch observes a static seeded sale offer, not the active run's generated offer
findings.summary: The watch page resolves its inventory target from an env knob defaulting to the seeded offer and never uses the recovery snapshot's currentRun.saleOfferId, while every run creates a fresh generated offer — so during any run the headline inventory-drain panels point at the wrong offer.

findings.title: Public run start promises a /watch redirect that never happens
findings.summary: The success toast says "Redirecting to watch…" but the handler returns immediately and only revalidates the home route; the operator stays on the home page and may believe the start silently failed.

findings.title: No client-side recovery re-fetch on SSE reconnect or terminal run events; recovery-sourced counts freeze for the whole watch session
findings.summary: Recovery is fetched once at server render and passed as a frozen prop; reconnects only flip a boolean and terminal run events are reducer no-ops, so events missed during a drop are permanently lost and the page never shows that the run ended — contradicting the documented recovery-on-reconnect contract.

findings.title: "Fail-closed" secret strength check accepts the committed dev sentinel; no startup validation forces an override
findings.summary: isSecretStrongEnough only checks byte length ≥ 16 and every committed change-me-* sentinel passes, so a deployment that forgets to override env silently mints admin sessions signed with a publicly known secret.

findings.title: Public "Demo Picker" cards are decorative: fictional preset slugs and no start action
findings.summary: The picker lists three slugs that exist as no preset and whose CTA is a bare link to /watch; the only real start is a separate panel hardcoded to preview-1k, so the documented public presets can be neither picked nor started from the picker.

findings.title: Stable error codes returned by every service are absent from the documented ERROR_CODES vocabulary
findings.summary: not_found (returned by all three services' 404 paths), delegation_failed, and the whole *_unavailable family the dashboard keys on are missing from the baseline, and ErrorPayloadSchema.code accepts any non-empty string, so drift validates silently.

findings.title: Worker readiness check notification_record_worker_running is contracted and documented but never emitted
findings.summary: The readiness vocabulary and docs advertise six worker checks but the service returns five; notification recording landed inline in order processing, so the documented separate worker loop never existed — vocabulary/docs drift that misleads operators and monitors.

findings.title: IsoTimestamp accepts any non-empty string, so timezone clarity is not enforced at the contract boundary
findings.summary: The shared timestamp schema is z.string().min(1); nothing catches a producer emitting a naive local timestamp or epoch value, though all producers emit UTC Z today. One central tightening would protect every boundary.

findings.title: OrderReadResponseSchema types order/reservation status as a free-form string instead of the canonical enum schemas
findings.summary: Both status fields are z.string().min(1) rather than the shared OrderStatusSchema/ReservationStatusSchema, so the read path can advertise a non-canonical lifecycle value — low impact today, but exactly the vocabulary-drift class the contracts exist to prevent.

findings.title: Documented per-package test commands do not exist
findings.summary: Five of the seven documented "Useful package commands" fail with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT (verified at runtime); the real contract is the root test:api/test:worker/test:integration/test:unit scripts, which the docs never point to.

findings.title: Load-orchestrator Dockerfile builds the entire workspace
findings.summary: An unfiltered pnpm build compiles every package (including the Next.js web bundle) into the load-orchestrator image build, unlike every other Dockerfile's scoped --filter form — wasted time and coupling to packages it never ships.

findings.title: Compose project names are not worktree-isolated despite the docs guaranteeing it
findings.summary: The default project name is a static branch-derived value, so two worktrees of the same branch share containers and volumes — one worktree's reset/wipe mutates the other's demo state, contrary to the documented isolation guarantee.

findings.title: infra:down tears down the whole project, not just PostgreSQL/Redis
findings.summary: infra:up scopes to the two data services but infra:down runs an unscoped docker compose down, stopping and removing the entire stack when an operator expects to stop only PostgreSQL and Redis.

findings.title: Caddy has no healthcheck, so runtime:up --wait can report success without proving the public entry point serves
findings.summary: Every other long-lived service has a healthcheck; caddy — the single public dashboard origin — is treated as ready as soon as its container is running.

findings.title: The only real-k6 behavioral test runs in the infrastructure-free unit lane and silently skips (suite stays green) whenever k6 is absent — which is the current state of this environment
findings.summary: k6-roundtrip.test.ts sits in the unit lane despite opening a TCP socket and spawning real k6, and degrades to it.skip when k6 is missing — verified to be the case here. The only assertions of real k6 compatibility and the sold-out failure_rate == 0 contract silently vanish while the suite reports green, and no load-orchestrator integration lane exists to move them to.

findings.title: x-load-run-id header-agreement matching/absent cases assert only the absence of a validation path, so they pass against a no-op header check
findings.summary: With db: undefined the request fails downstream regardless, so asserting the error paths don't contain runId cannot distinguish an accepted match from an unrelated failure; only the sibling mismatch case pins the detection.
